title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with a synthetic video call. Someone used a deepfake to appear as a sitting chief minister on WhatsApp, then extended the same impersonation to a second fake official, a supposed CBI officer demanding a fine. The failure sits at the point of contact between a citizen and a person claiming state authority, on a consumer messaging app, not inside any government system. No part of the exchange passed through a channel where the claimed identity could be checked.

What would have caught it is a verification step independent of the call itself. The victim's only evidence that he was dealing with a chief minister was the video call, and his only evidence for the officer was the officer's own claim. The demands for exchange charges, a PIN unlock fee and a fine were the visible structure of the fraud, and each one was paid without any confirmation that the office or the aid programme existed.

The reporting does not establish who operated the deepfake, whether anyone was arrested, or that the person depicted had any knowledge of the calls. A case registered under the Information Technology Act is a complaint, not a finding.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29 year old security guard in Bengaluru, Ratikanta Giri, lost more than Rs 1.04 lakh after a WhatsApp video call used an AI deepfake to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and actor C Joseph Vijay. On Sept 9, the caller promised Rs 11 lakh in financial aid. A supposed manager then asked for fees, including Rs 5,000 as exchange charges and Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN.

Later, someone claiming to be CBI officer Thakur demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine. Giri paid through a digital payment app until the fraudsters asked for another Rs 50,000, when he refused and realized he had been duped. He contacted cybercrime helpline 1930 and then Byappanahalli police. Police registered a case under the Information Technology Act and urged people not to trust such calls or make payments based on them.
